html:
Damdin Sükhbaatar was a Mongolian revolutionary who led the partisan army in the revolution of 1921. Mongolia's communist state honoured him as the father of its revolution.

He had served as a soldier in the army of the newly independent Mongolia under the Bogd Khan. In 1919 and 1920 Chinese troops took the country back, then the White Russian warlord Ungern-Sternberg seized the capital. Sükhbaatar, with Choibalsan and others, founded the Mongolian People's Party and asked Soviet Russia for help. In July 1921 his partisans and the Red Army took the capital, then called Khüree.

He became minister of war but died in 1923, aged thirty. The capital's main square was named after him, and many link the city's new name, Ulaanbaatar, "red hero", to him. In 1990 that same square filled with crowds calling for democracy.
sum: Damdin Sükhbaatar was a Mongolian revolutionary who led the partisan army in the revolution of 1921. Mongolia's communist state honoured him as the father of its revolution.
